extracted.intended_audience: Prospective AAAI-25 authors submitting to the main technical track and affiliated special tracks (AI Alignment, AI for Social Impact)
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a double-blind research paper (abstract + full paper) to the AAAI-25 main technical track (including AI Alignment and AI for Social Impact tracks) following conference rules on registration, formatting, page limits, ethics, reproducibility, and concurrent-submission policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author registration and account
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must register at the AAAI-25 web-based technical track paper submission site before they can submit abstracts and papers. Authors are required to use the same OpenReview account (i.e., associated with the same email address) across all submissions and review assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid last-minute congestion, authors are encouraged to register well in advance of the abstract deadline. IMPORTANT: Authors must enter the names of ALL AUTHORS at the time of registration (by abstract deadline) — OpenReview includes a hard-coded note that this is optional, however, this is a mandatory step for AAAI-25 authors. According to AAAI policy, all author names must be added at the time of abstract registration, and the list of names as well as the order in which they appear cannot be changed after August 15. In addition, the contact author and contact information cannot be changed after the abstract submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract + full paper required
rubrics_metrics.description: Every submission requires both an abstract submission and a corresponding paper submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For regular papers, abstracts must be submitted by August 7, 2024 and full papers must be submitted by August 15, 2024. There will be no individual exceptions. If you experience technical problems with OpenReview contact workflowchairs25@aaai.zendesk.com. Submissions will not be accepted by e-mail or any other mechanism other than OpenReview. After submission, the system will not automatically send a confirmation of receipt; to receive a confirmation email click the paper ID then the 'Email' button. The submission system will be closed exactly at the deadline with no individual exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines are UTC-12 (Anywhere on Earth) and no exceptions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are track-specific and may differ from the main-track dates; track-specific deadlines are listed on respective CFP pages. Once a deadline passes, AAAI will be unable to make individual exceptions or correspond with authors about circumstances that prevented timely submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: No placeholder or vacuous abstracts/titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions that have “placeholder” (e.g., test or xyz) titles or abstracts (or none at all) will be deleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors of such vacuous submissions will be notified that their abstract has been deleted and will not be allowed to submit a full paper. The Program Chairs also reserve the right to reject papers without review if they change their abstracts substantially between the abstract and final deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting: AAAI two-column camera-ready style and PDF requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be formatted in AAAI two-column, camera-ready style and must be in trouble-free, high-resolution PDF format, formatted for US Letter (8.5" x 11") paper, using Type 1 or TrueType fonts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the AAAI-25 author kit for details. Only PDF files are required at the time of submission for review; authors will additionally need to submit paper source files if their paper is accepted for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI submissions are anonymous and must conform to the instructions for double-blind review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must remove all author and affiliation information from their submission for review, and may replace it with other information, such as paper number and keywords. Acknowledgements should be omitted from papers submitted for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits (content vs references) and acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions may consist of up to 7 pages of technical content plus additional pages solely for references; acknowledgements should be omitted from papers submitted for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reproducibility checklist (added after references) will not count toward the page limit. Further technical details (proofs, assumptions, algorithm pseudocode) may be included in a Technical Appendix or Code and Data Appendix as appropriate; follow the author kit for how to include appendices/supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material and code deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material and code are due separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary material and code must be submitted by August 19, 2024. Information related to reproducing experimental results may be included in the main paper or the Code and Data Appendix, as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission limit per author
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual author is limited to no more than a combined limit of 10 submissions to the AAAI-25 technical track (including AI Alignment and AI for Social Impact tracks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may not be added to papers following submission (see policies about author changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for changes to titles/authors after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications to submissions are only allowed until the full paper deadline (August 15 for Phase 1 submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No exceptions will be granted. See the full Paper Modification Guidelines for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-submission / prior-publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI-25 will not consider any paper that, at the time of submission, is under review or has already been published or accepted for publication in any archival venue such as a journal or a conference (workshops and preprint servers such as arXiv are acceptable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are free to retract a submission from a venue with a concurrent review process and submit the same work to AAAI-25 provided the retraction occurs before the AAAI-25 submission. Authors must confirm at time of submission that the paper is not under review at another archival conference or journal. Once submitted to AAAI-25, authors may not submit the same paper to another archival conference or journal until they receive an accept/reject decision from AAAI-25 or they withdraw their submission from AAAI-25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling suspected excessive overlap / summary reject process
rubrics_metrics.description: If a concern is raised about the similarity of two non-identical submissions, at least three people will inspect whatever information is available about both submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If they all agree that the simultaneous submission has excessive technical overlap, the paper will be summarily rejected and the organizers of the other conference will be informed about AAAI’s decision. As with all summary rejects, such decisions are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and comparison expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are expected to cite those refereed publications most relevant to their content, but authors are excused for not knowing about all non-refereed work (e.g., appearing on arXiv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases where prior (non-refereed) work is widely known in the field, its existence may be considered by reviewers when assessing novelty. Papers published less than two months before the regular paper submission deadline (August 15, 2024) are considered contemporaneous to all AAAI-25 submissions; authors are not obliged to address such papers (though they are encouraged to do so for camera-ready versions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility checklist requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must complete a reproducibility checklist at the time of paper submission, which outlines how to reproduce the results of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include your answers in your PDF after the references; this will not count toward the page limit. The checklist responses will become part of each paper submission and will be shared with reviewers. Reviewers will be asked to assess the degree to which the results reported are reproducible, and this assessment will be weighed when making final decisions. Authors are encouraged to include detailed reproducibility information in the Technical Appendix and Code and Data Appendix as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and professional conduct compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All AAAI authors and reviewers are required to honor the AAAI Publications Ethics and Malpractice Statement, as well as the AAAI Code of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A paper may be rejected if an author is found to violate the Publications Ethics and Malpractice Statement or the Code of Professional Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration interest and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: During paper submission, authors may express interest in giving a public demo of systems described in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on expressions of interest and on reviews, papers will be selected to participate in a demonstration session, which will occur in addition to technical talks and posters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author expectation to join reviewer pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the size of the conference, all authors of AAAI-25 submissions will be expected to join the conference’s reviewer pool unless prevented by extenuating circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential reviewers will be vetted based on their research experience, and depending on this experience may be selected as program committee or senior program committee members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source files required for camera-ready
rubrics_metrics.description: Only PDF files are required at the time of submission for review; authors will additionally need to submit paper source files if their paper is accepted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and retain source files; follow camera-ready instructions in the author kit if accepted.
